gen-fs-sharpie-lora: Sharpie's letters nearly close up, leaving a hairline crack, like text glimpsed through a narrow slot. Lora opens back up with a broad, welcoming c, made for brief reading, while Sharpie earns its keep big and short.
gen-fs-striper-lora: Striper is graphic and playful, with low contrast across the alphabet. Striper is best on a few words, while Lora, a literary serif with a broad, welcoming c, is best when the text keeps going.
gen-fs-telma-fs-bespoke-slab: Understated and graceful, Telma writes flowing pen letters with a wide-mouthed a and a high mean line across every word. Bespoke Slab, a tall-bodied serif, wants generous size for brief reading.
gen-fs-telma-fs-technor: Graceful and understated, Telma flows with pen-written letters under a high mean line. And Technor, glowing like neon tubing, is built for brief reading, its thread-thin line stitched along a path.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-amulya: Autour One leads with a clear channel into every round letter, bold and expressive, with hardly any step down from capitals. Autour One grabs attention; Amulya, with generous curves, carries the talking.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-chillax: Autour One is bold and expressive, with a clear channel leading into each round letter. But Chillax relaxes things with a spaghetti-like line and pen-lifted curves left pleasantly unfinished.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-plein: Autour One joins its strokes without any thinning or bulging. It makes the bold statement, while Plein, a reliable sans-serif with clean round openings, handles the steady reading.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-roundo: Expressive and bold, Autour One has a clear channel leading into each round letter. And Roundo, geometric, keeps its n arch matched to the stem and every small counter unclogged.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-spline-sans: Bold, expressive shapes lead, with a clear channel into every round letter. Spline Sans settles things with wide gaps between curve ends and stems, and identical weight in verticals and horizontals.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-synonym: Below the bold Autour One, the text reads dependably, a constant stripe of ink. Synonym would hold up page after page, its generous curve openings never clogging as the lines pile up.
